subject.summary: The Russian Soyuz MS crewed spacecraft in orbit: spherical orbital module with its docking probe, bell-shaped descent module, cylindrical service module with its main engine, two four-panel solar arrays and the Kurs rendezvous antennas. Assembled as a diagram, not a launch sequence.

sources.title: The user's request

identity.feature: Spherical orbital module with the 8-latch docking ring and its crown-headed probe at the very front
Bell-shaped descent module, widest at the heat shield, with the crew porthole and the Vzor sight
Cylindrical service module with the forward skirt, the four thruster packs and the KTDU main engine bell
Two four-panel solar wings on rotary drives, 10.6 m tip to tip
Two parabolic Kurs dishes on stalks above the shoulder

next: The viewer clamps the staged build to 20 s (assembly.seconds <= 20), so the build cannot fill a 60 s piece at 1x: drive it from the film clock (t = 0.36 x wallclock over the first 55 s) or render frames with ?t=.
Fold the two wings stowed and deploy them with articulations: that is the true in-orbit build story and would give the last third of the piece its own event.
Density on the descent module: the bell's blanket still needs seam belts, hatch dogs and umbilical fairings at 0.6x grid weight (critic round 2, defect 1).
The docking interface should read as an aperture with eight cleats rather than a flat plated ring (critic round 2, defects 2-4).
A rail-level pass on the solar panels: diagonal lattice inside each panel face and six cell rows (critic round 2, defect 5).

The critic measured the reference as OM 2.98 m / SM 2.26 m against this scene's 2.66 / 2.62; that photo is foreshortened at the docking end and the documented figures support the split as built. A clean orthographic drawing would settle it.
One visible life cue in a still: raise the motes and give the beacon a slow pulse (critic round 2, defect 10).
